target_customer: Small food, retail and service businesses in Southeast Asia and beyond that take orders through WhatsApp
problem: Small merchants take orders by chat and lose time to manual order taking, payments and admin. Take App gives them a store link that sends structured orders to WhatsApp.
business_model: Freemium SaaS subscription (free tier, $29 and $50 monthly plans) with no commission on sales

founders.name: Youmin Kim
prior_employers: Facebook (engineering manager who launched Facebook Marketplace and Messaging Commerce in Southeast Asia)
founders.background_notes: Per YC page. TechCrunch calls him a former Facebook engineering manager. Education not found. The company about page says he built the first version over a weekend during the 2020 Singapore lockdown.

competitors.name: Charles
competitors.what: German conversational commerce and newsletters on WhatsApp for Europe

technical_complexity.rationale: A store and order form that forwards structured messages to WhatsApp is standard web engineering; payments and automation add moderate work.

defensibility.rationale: Merchants' store links and order history create mild lock in, but the core feature was easy to copy and depends on WhatsApp.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Meta invested through its NPE team in 2022 rather than copying; PYMNTS reported Meta pushing into restaurant ordering on WhatsApp. No source seen on a Meta product that displaced Take App.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (August 2022) reported about 1,000 businesses across 35 markets, mostly restaurants in Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia, using Take App. Pandemic lockdowns pushed small sellers to chat ordering.

branding.domain_note: take.app, a short exact app TLD domain (acquisition details not found)

identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly and practical, benefit focused headlines such as 'Less admin. More time to grow.'

branding.brand_signature: The take.app short domain and the 'Shopify for WhatsApp commerce' positioning
branding.community_and_virality: Meta backing was covered by TechCrunch, PYMNTS and other outlets in August 2022, and the site lists press and merchant case studies.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic descriptive name with a good domain, but no mascot, merch or community evidence. Press was about the Meta investment, not the brand.

outcome_analysis: Take App is active. It started as a free, nonprofit style tool in Singapore, raised a $1M seed in June 2022 with YC and Meta, and now claims 300,000 plus merchants in 180 plus countries on a freemium subscription. Growth is helped by the free tier and by riding WhatsApp's reach, with the main risk being platform dependency on Meta. Customer counts are self reported. In 2023 it took over users of Orderdulu when that service closed.
notes: Seed of $1M reported by TechCrunch (2022-08-15) and on the YC page news; the round closed quietly in June 2022. CB Insights lists $1.5M total, source of the extra amount not found, treated as unverified. Meta's share of the round is not stated. Founded year 2021 per YC, though the company about page describes starting as a nonprofit during the 2020 lockdown. The Charles competitor entry is from an article dated after the batch (August 2022), noted as within months. The vulcanpost piece was corrected to say Take App took over Orderdulu users rather than acquiring the company.
